cohort: The participants were 116 women undergoing in-vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET), divided into an anti-SSA/SSB antibodies-positive group (n=55) and an anti-SSA/SSB antibodies-negative control group (n=61).
finding: Women with anti-SSA/SSB antibodies showed higher levels of inflammatory cytokines, lower levels of certain immune cells, and experienced significantly poorer IVF outcomes (including lower oocyte/embryo yields and quality) and reduced clinical pregnancy, implantation, take-home baby rates, and birth weight.
